title: Elijah
hook: When Elijah storms onto the biblical stage without introduction or genealogy, announcing a drought that will last years, he's doing far more than delivering bad news—he's declaring war on the storm god himself. While Baal's prophets claimed their deity controlled rain and fertility, the God of Israel was about to demonstrate who truly commands the skies. But the most startling truth of Elijah's story isn't the spectacular fire from heaven or the confrontation at Carmel; it's what happens after his greatest victory, when the prophet who called down divine fire flees into the wilderness, suicidal and broken, certain he's failed. In that cave at Horeb, God will teach his exhausted servant that divine power doesn't always arrive in earthquake and flame—sometimes it whispers in stillness, and sometimes one faithful life matters more than we can possibly imagine. This week's chapters take us into the heart of Israel's darkest apostasy and introduce us to the man who learned that prophetic ministry is less about dramatic miracles than about standing, often alone, in the place God assigns.
